2607.02073.title: Evidence-State Rewards for Long-Context Reasoning
2607.02073.paper_summary: Long-context reasoning requires models to locate, revise, and synthesize evidence distributed across lengthy inputs. Existing long-context RL methods usually reward final answers or static evidence extraction, offering little feedback on how intermediate actions change the model's evidence state. We propose Maven, a reinforcement learning framework with an editable evidence memory. Maven defines an answer-conditioned evidence-state value and rewards action-level state transitions: add actions are credited by marginal gain and hindsight contribution, link actions by evidence synergy, and drop actions by improved answer support after removing misleading evidence. These rewards are assigned to the corresponding action spans in GRPO. Across Llama and Qwen models on LongBench v2, LongReason, and RULER, Maven outperforms outcome-only RL and evidence-identification baselines, producing more sufficient evidence sets and lower distractor retention. Our results show that long-context RL benefits from optimizing stateful evidence navigation rather than one-shot evidence extraction.
2607.02073.paper_summary_zh: 長期上下文推理要求模型在冗長的輸入中定位、修訂和綜合分散的證據。現有的長期上下文強化學習方法通常僅對最終答案或靜態證據提取給予獎勵，對於中間行動如何改變模型的證據狀態幾乎沒有反饋。我們提出了Maven，一個具有可編輯證據記憶的強化學習框架。Maven定義了一個基於答案的證據狀態值，並對行動層級的狀態轉換給予獎勵：添加行動根據邊際收益和事後貢獻獲得積分，鏈接行動根據證據協同獲得獎勵，刪除行動則是在去除誤導性證據後提高答案支持。這些獎勵被分配到GRPO中的相應行動範圍。在LongBench v2、LongReason和RULER上的Llama和Qwen模型中，Maven超越了僅依賴結果的強化學習和證據識別基準，產生了更充分的證據集和更低的干擾保留。我們的結果顯示，長期上下文強化學習受益於優化有狀態的證據導航，而非一次性證據提取。
2607.02073.author: Ya Gao et.al.
